paragraphs.title: Esther Approaches the King and Is Invited to Ask

easy.explanation: Esther put on her royal apparel.
easy.q: What did Esther put on when she stood in the inner court of the king’s house?

answers: In the inner court of the king’s house
easy.explanation: She stood in the inner court of the king’s house.
The king held out the golden sceptre to her.
easy.q: What did the king hold out to Esther?

answers: She touched the top of the sceptre
medium.explanation: Esther drew near and touched the top of the sceptre.
medium.q: What did Esther do after the king held out the sceptre?

answers: She obtained favour in his sight
Haman had asked him to do so
medium.explanation: Esther obtained favour in the king’s sight.
medium.q: Why could the king invite Esther to make her request?

answers: The king was angry with her
The king did not notice her
The king looked on her with approval
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the king received Esther favorably.
medium.q: What does the phrase “she obtained favour in his sight” mean?

challenge.explanation: The king held out the golden sceptre before Esther drew near.
challenge.q: What action by the king allowed Esther to draw near to him?

challenge.explanation: The king asked what her request was and promised to grant it.
challenge.q: What did the king invite Esther to do?

answers: That the king rejected her request
The king’s willingness to grant a very great request
challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses an exaggerated promise of generosity.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “even to the half of the kingdom” emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The First Banquet and the Delayed Request

easy.explanation: Esther invited the king and Haman.
easy.q: Whom did Esther invite to the first banquet?

answers: Yes, at the beginning of the banquet
easy.explanation: Esther did not state her request at the first banquet.
easy.q: Did Esther state her request immediately at the first banquet?

answers: At the end of that day
easy.explanation: Esther said that she would do so tomorrow.
easy.q: When did Esther say she would do as the king had said?

answers: He came to the banquet with Haman
medium.explanation: The king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared.
medium.q: What did the king do after Esther invited him and Haman?

answers: She postponed the request until another banquet
medium.explanation: She invited them to another banquet on the next day.
medium.q: What did Esther do after the king asked her at the banquet what her request was?

answers: The place where Esther was sitting
The thing Esther was asking for
medium.explanation: Her request was the matter she wanted the king to grant.
medium.q: In this context, what does “my request” mean?

answers: The second banquet, the invitation to Haman, and the king’s question
The invitation to the king and Haman, the first banquet, and the delayed request
The delayed request, the king’s arrival, and the invitation to Haman
challenge.explanation: Esther invited them, they came to the banquet, and she postponed her request.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of events?

answers: She had not yet stated her request
She asked Haman to hold the banquet
challenge.explanation: The additional banquet came before she stated her request.
challenge.q: What does Esther’s repeated invitation to the king and Haman show?

answers: She was angry with the king
challenge.explanation: Esther postponed her request and proceeded cautiously.
challenge.q: Which description best fits Esther’s actions in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Haman’s Joy and His Anger at Mordecai

answers: Joyful and with a glad heart
easy.explanation: Haman went forth joyful and with a glad heart.
easy.q: How did Haman leave the banquet?

easy.explanation: Haman saw Mordecai at the king’s gate.
easy.q: Whom did Haman see at the king’s gate?

easy.explanation: Haman was full of indignation against Mordecai.
easy.q: What happened to Haman when he saw Mordecai?

answers: Mordecai did not stand or move before him
medium.explanation: Mordecai’s refusal to rise or move angered Haman.
medium.q: Why did Haman’s joy change to anger?

medium.explanation: Haman restrained himself and went home.
medium.q: What did Haman do instead of acting immediately in anger?

answers: He restrained himself and controlled his actions
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Haman held himself back from acting immediately.

answers: He leaves joyful but becomes angry because of Mordecai
He leaves sad but becomes joyful at home
He is angry with Esther but praises Mordecai
challenge.explanation: Haman’s joy changes to indignation when he sees Mordecai.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in Haman’s behavior in these verses?

answers: He called for his friends and Zeresh
He sent a message to Mordecai
challenge.explanation: He sent and called for his friends and Zeresh his wife.
challenge.q: What did Haman do when he came home?

answers: Mordecai did not stand up or move for him
challenge.explanation: The text specifically says that Mordecai did not stand up or move for Haman.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Mordecai did not change his behavior toward Haman?

paragraphs.title: Haman Boasts but Finds No Satisfaction

easy.explanation: Haman told them about his riches, children, honor, and position.
easy.q: What did Haman tell his friends and Zeresh about?

easy.explanation: Haman boasted that Esther the queen had invited him.
easy.q: Who had invited Haman to banquets with the king?

answers: All his achievements while he saw Mordecai
easy.explanation: All his success meant nothing to him while Mordecai remained before him.
easy.q: What did Haman say was worth nothing to him?

answers: The king had advanced him above the princes and servants
Esther had given him the palace
medium.explanation: Haman said the king had advanced him above the princes and servants.
medium.q: What did Haman say about the honor the king had given him?

answers: Mordecai still sat at the king’s gate and did not honor him
He had not been invited to the first banquet
medium.explanation: Mordecai’s presence and refusal to honor him spoiled Haman’s satisfaction.
medium.q: Why was Haman still dissatisfied despite his success?

medium.explanation: In this context, glory refers to honor, splendor, and high status.
medium.q: What does “glory” mean in Haman’s description of his riches?

answers: Esther’s invitation caused him to lose his wealth
Mordecai’s lack of honor kept Haman from being satisfied
His children caused him to leave his home
challenge.explanation: Although Haman had great success, Mordecai’s behavior kept him from satisfaction.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in Haman’s words?

answers: Esther did not invite the king
Esther invited Haman with the king to another banquet
Mordecai invited him to his house
challenge.explanation: Haman especially noted that he was invited with the king again on the next day.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes Haman’s special invitation?

answers: Haman valued none of his achievements when Mordecai did not honor him
Haman gave up all his position
Haman was pleased that Mordecai sat at the gate
challenge.explanation: Mordecai’s refusal to honor him mattered more to Haman than all his achievements.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the words “all this availeth me nothing”?

paragraphs.title: Zeresh’s Proposal and the Preparation of the Gallows

easy.explanation: Zeresh and all Haman’s friends made the suggestion.
easy.q: Who suggested that the gallows should be made?

easy.explanation: They told Haman to speak to the king in the morning.
easy.q: To whom did they suggest that Haman should speak about hanging Mordecai?

answers: He caused the gallows to be made
easy.explanation: Haman accepted the idea and caused the gallows to be made.
easy.q: What did Haman do after the idea pleased him?

medium.explanation: They proposed gallows fifty cubits high.
medium.q: How high were the gallows they proposed?

medium.explanation: They told him to speak to the king on the next morning.
medium.q: When did they tell Haman to speak to the king?

answers: The idea found favor with Haman
Haman did not understand the idea
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Haman liked the proposed plan.
medium.q: What does “the thing pleased Haman” mean?

answers: Go to the banquet, build the gallows, and then speak to the king
Speak to the king in the morning, hang Mordecai, and then go merrily to the banquet
Invite Mordecai, build the gallows, and cancel the banquet
challenge.explanation: The proposal was to ask the king in the morning, hang Mordecai, and then attend the banquet joyfully.
challenge.q: What was the order of actions proposed to Haman?

challenge.explanation: The text says that the thing pleased Haman.
challenge.q: Why did Haman accept Zeresh’s proposal?

answers: To provide a place for the banquet
challenge.explanation: The gallows were intended for hanging Mordecai.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of making the gallows?
